final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly confirmed that controls alone, the draft risk acceptance, and unconditional certification are unsupported. That clarification is directionally consistent with the initial audit view, but it is a reinterpretation of the same record rather than evidence that the required compliance predicate has been satisfied. The governing policy allows rollout controls and monitoring to mitigate a model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable; the raw evidence shows neither. The policy and evidence also support that disclosure is required when the limitation remains unresolved and exposed, but there is still no admissible proof that the required pre-launch model-card disclosure actually exists or that certification has been formally conditioned on it. Because those initial concerns were not closed by genuinely new admissible evidence, the appropriate final status remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still supports only a conditional certification theory tied to explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure, not a presently supported certification outcome.
The affected energy outage response segment still remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, so the policy predicate for mitigation by rollout controls is still unmet.
The cited risk acceptance remains only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the exposed outage segment.
The recommended action still overcompresses the required condition because there is no admissible launch-approval artifact showing certification is expressly conditioned on disclosure before release.
